# Module `png`

png - a minimal PNG encoder, in pure Vyb.

Turns a flat 8-bit RGB pixel buffer into a standards-valid PNG: signature,
`IHDR` (bit depth 8, colour type 2), one `IDAT` holding a zlib stream with
STORED (uncompressed) DEFLATE blocks, and `IEND`. No compression, no filter
heuristics, no runtime/C dependency -- the container itself, with correct
chunk CRCs and an adler32 stream checksum, is what this module produces.

Stored blocks are deliberate: they keep the encoder pure Vyb and deterministic
(the DEFLATE stream is byte-identical for identical pixels), at the cost of
file size. A fit-for-purpose choice for fixtures, screenshots and test images;
a compressed encoder would need a matching DEFLATE writer in `archive`.

Pixel buffer convention: one byte per channel, row-major, three bytes per
pixel -- `Vec<UInt8>` of length `w * h * 3`, exactly the flat RGB buffer
`io::write_bytes` and the #213 binary surface already speak.

  import png::{png_rgb_fill, png_rgb_set, png_encode, png_write}
  buf<Vec<UInt8>> = png_rgb_fill(64, 64, 0xFFFFFF)     # white canvas
  png_rgb_set(borrow(buf), 64, 10, 10, 0xD31E1E)       # red pixel at (10,10)
  png_write("/tmp/out.png", 64, 64, buf)               # persist

CRC32 and adler32 are computed in-module (RANGE-checked CRC32 for a chunk's
type+data, unlike `archive::crc32`, which covers a whole buffer), so `png`
depends only on `io` for the write path.

<a id="sym-png_crc32"></a>
### `png_crc32` · fn

```
png_crc32(v<Vec<UInt8>>, a<Int>, b<Int>)<Int> ->
```

CRC32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320) over bytes [a, b) of `v`.
The range matters: a PNG chunk CRC covers the 4 type bytes AND the payload, so
the caller passes `[chunkStart + 4, chunkStart + 4 + 4 + payloadLen)`.

<a id="sym-png_encode"></a>
### `png_encode` · fn

```
png_encode(w<Int>, h<Int>, rgb<Vec<UInt8>>)<Vec<UInt8>> ->
```

Encode `rgb` (w * h * 3 bytes, row-major RGB) as a PNG byte buffer. Returns an
empty buffer when the geometry or the pixel-buffer length is invalid, so a
caller can check `.len() == 0` instead of trusting a malformed file.

The whole byte buffer is built inside this function: a `Vec<UInt8>` must not
cross a function boundary on this build (see io's binary surface notes).

<a id="sym-png_rgb_set"></a>
### `png_rgb_set` · fn

```
png_rgb_set(buf<their<Vec<UInt8>>>, w<Int>, x<Int>, y<Int>, color<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Set the pixel at (x, y) in a `w`-wide buffer to packed 0xRRGGBB `color`.
Mutates in place, so the caller passes `borrow(buf)`. Returns 0 on success,
1 when the coordinates are outside the buffer.

<a id="sym-png_write"></a>
### `png_write` · fn

```
png_write(path<String>, w<Int>, h<Int>, rgb<Vec<UInt8>>)<Bool?> ->
```

Write the PNG for `rgb` to `path`. Present on success; absent when the PNG
could not be built or the file could not be opened/written.
